evals.name: library-add-album-silent-failure
evals.prompt: In my SwiftUI app, I fetch an Album from MusicCatalogSearchRequest and let the user tap 'Save to Library'. The handler does `try await MusicLibrary.shared.add(album, to: playlist)`. The call doesn't throw, but when the user opens the Music app afterward, the playlist is empty — no songs got added, no error shown anywhere. What's going on and how do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses the root cause as passing the bare Album container into add(_:to:) instead of its resolved contents — the call silently produces an empty identifier set rather than throwing. States the catalog-identifier rule: items must trace back to a catalog fetch. Fix fetches/extracts the Album's contents (e.g. via album.with(.tracks)) and adds those items individually — either as Song (from a direct catalog search) or as Track (from the album's tracks relationship); Track does NOT need to be unwrapped into Song, since Track conforms to MusicPlaylistAddable directly per Apple's own docs and carries its own populated identifier set when catalog-sourced. Does NOT attribute the failure to authorization, network, or a generic 'add error handling' fix without naming the container-vs-contents mismatch.
expectations: Identifies that passing the bare Album container (rather than its resolved Song/Track contents) to add(_:to:) is the actual root cause, not authorization/network/missing error handling
Names the mechanism as an empty identifier set / silent no-op, not a thrown error
The proposed fix adds individual catalog-sourced items (Song from search, or Track from the album's tracks relationship) instead of the bare Album
Does not propose a generic try/catch or null-check as the primary fix, and does NOT falsely require unwrapping Track into Song (Track is directly addable)

evals.name: speech-musickit-tap-crash
evals.prompt: My app has a voice-command feature using SFSpeechRecognizer with an AVAudioEngine input tap, and separately plays music via ApplicationMusicPlayer. Ever since I added a 'while you were listening, want to play this?' flow that triggers playback right after a voice command, the app crashes with `CreateRecordingTap: nullptr == Tap()` sometimes when the same view triggers both features close together. What's causing this and how do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: Identifies this as a Speech + MusicKit audio-session/tap coexistence conflict, not a MusicKit playback bug in isolation. Names the specific mechanism: installing a new recording tap on the audio engine while a previous tap is still installed (double-installTap), or starting MusicKit playback while the speech recording session hasn't been fully torn down. Fix requires a full teardown sequence before any MusicKit call: removeTap before every installTap, stop the audio engine, end the recognition request, and enforce a single-flow rule so speech recording and playback never run concurrently (e.g. an isRecording guard).
expectations: Identifies this as an audio-session/tap conflict between Speech and MusicKit, not an isolated MusicKit bug
Names double-installTap or an incomplete teardown (missing removeTap/engine stop) as the mechanism
Fix includes a full stop/removeTap/end-request sequence before any MusicKit call
Recommends a guard so speech recording and playback don't run concurrently (single-flow rule)

evals.name: generic-icerror-unknown-triage
evals.prompt: Users are reporting that MusicKit search sometimes just fails. In our crash reporting all I see is `error.localizedDescription` = 'unknown error' or sometimes empty. I don't have any more detail than that. How do I actually figure out what's wrong before I try to fix it?
evals.expected_output: Does not guess a specific fix from the symptom string alone. Instead prescribes a diagnostic-first step: before proposing any fix, instrument the catch block around the failing call (e.g. MusicCatalogSearchRequest.response()) to capture and log the NSError's domain, code, and any NSUnderlyingErrorKey value, then reproduce the failure once to read the actual domain/code. Only after that should it map the domain/code to a specific cause (e.g. ICErrorDomain -8200/-8102/-7010/-7013) and a targeted fix. Also notes the diagnostic should be removed before merging (debugging probe, not production telemetry).
expectations: Does not jump straight to a specific guessed fix (e.g. 'it's probably auth' or 'it's probably network') without first getting more diagnostic information
Explicitly recommends capturing/logging the NSError domain, code, and underlying error before proposing a fix
Frames this as a required step prior to any targeted fix, not an optional nice-to-have
Mentions removing the diagnostic once the root cause is found (not leaving it as production code)
